raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Two small FROST cleanups, one commit each.

## 1. `test(sdpa)`: re-record the two sm107 d256 rendering pins that #1547 moved

### Symptom

On `develop`, two rendering-md5 pins in `test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm107.py` fail wherever `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.8.0 knows `sm_107a` (they trace-compile on the host, no GPU needed):

* `test_sm107_thd_gate_descriptor_leaves_the_dense_gated_and_ungated_thd_cubins_byte_identical` (`_THD_GATE_CUBIN_RECORD`): `dense_gated_bf16_lse` renders `fde505d0...`, the record says `50657ada...`
* `test_shared_d256_body_gate_seams_leave_every_ungated_rendering_byte_identical_on_both_archs` (`_PAGED_GATE_CUBIN_RECORD`): `sm_100a_dense` `dc698e8b... -> 7db6daaf...`, `sm_107a_dense` `b4af8e7d... -> 63d9b3ef...`

### Cause

#1547 (`bdf93dbb3`) changed the shared d256 f16 prefill body on the dense CLC path (one scheduler publisher, `read_tile_id_arrive_on_leader`, under `not CFG.THD_VARLEN`) and re-recorded only the d512 renderings. The two pins here exist so that a HOST-side feature (the THD gate descriptor, the paged gate seams) cannot move the body unnoticed; a deliberate body change re-records them.

### Attribution (measured, not inferred)

With the tests' own probes (host trace-compiles, DSL 4.8.0): at `bdf93dbb3~1` all five arms of interest render their recorded md5s; at `bdf93dbb3` exactly the three dense arms render the new ones, and those equal what `develop` renders today -- no later commit moved them again. Every THD / paged / gated arm (the ten other keys) still renders its record, as the `THD_VARLEN` guard predicts.

### Change

The three md5s, re-recorded under the same DSL, plus one provenance comment per record. Test-only.

## 2. `fix(gated_attention_block)`: the cache-write launcher pins every operand to `src_a`'s CUDA device

### Symptom

`run_cache_write` validated dtype, rank, extents, strides and alignment but never the device: `check_pool` / `check_slot_mapping` were called without their `device=` argument. A CPU `slot_mapping` -- a serving stack's `torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int32)` with no `device=` -- passed every launcher check and reached the compiled call. The served route was already guarded (the block's execute preflight pins the pools and the slot mapping to the plan's device through the same helpers); the gap was the launcher's standalone contract, which the kernel tests and downstream launchers use directly.

### Change

The launcher requires `src_a.is_cuda`, `src_b` on `src_a`'s device, and passes `src_a.device` to `check_pool` (both pools) and `check_slot_mapping` -- the helpers' existing parameter and messages (`<name> must live on <device>, got cpu`). `is_cuda` alone cannot tell a tensor on another GPU from a local one, hence the comparison by device. Host attributes only: nothing is read back from the device (Rule 3), and the check raises `ValueError` by name instead of converting (Rule 1).

### Test

Four refusals appended to `test_block_serving_extend.py::test_kernel_runner_refuses_a_mismatched_binding` (L0, any GPU): CPU `slot_mapping`, CPU `pool_b`, CPU `src_b`, CPU `src_a`.

## Evidence

Host = an A100 (cc 8.0) box, Python 3.10, torch 2.13.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, cuDNN 9.27; the Rubin / Blackwell device cells skip there, the host pins (trace-compiles) and the arch-neutral cache-write cells run.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| the two pin tests on the unchanged tree | RED: 2 failed (the three md5s above) |
| the two pin tests at this head | GREEN: 2 passed; all 13 printed md5s equal the records |
| attribution probe (five arms at `bdf93dbb3~1` / `bdf93dbb3`) | 5 / 5 match the records before #1547; exactly the 3 dense arms move at #1547, to the md5s `develop` renders today |
| `test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm107.py`, `-m "L0 or L1"`, at this head | 216 passed, 439 skipped (Rubin / Blackwell device cells on an A100), 0 failed in 293 s -- every other rendering pin of the module unchanged |
| `test_kernel_runner_refuses_a_mismatched_binding` on the unchanged launcher (test hunk only) | RED: 1 failed -- the CPU slot passed every launcher check and reached the compiled call, whose own argument check stopped it with a message naming an argument position, not the operand |
| the same cell at this head | GREEN: 1 passed (185 s incl. the arch-neutral compile) |
| the ten gated-block modules that use the launcher + `core/test_import_boundaries.py`, `-m "L0 or L1"`, at this head | 263 passed, 322 skipped (every skip = the Rubin-only accept marker on an A100), 0 failed in 248 s |
| `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files | black / black-jupyter / SPDX passed, nothing reformatted |

     t = int(src_a.shape[0])
     if src_b is not None and int(src_b.shape[0]) != t:
         raise ValueError(f"src_a and src_b must carry the same T, got {t} and {int(src_b.shape[0])}")
-    check_pool(pool_a, "pool_a", h=r.h, page_size=r.page_size, d=r.d, dtype=r.dtype)

+    if not src_a.is_cuda:

+    if src_b is not None and src_b.device != src_a.device:

     if slot.dtype != r.slot_dtype:

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `31c475acb59f` against base `de9d698af0cc`.

No findings. The device checks close the standalone cache-write launcher's preflight gap without changing the kernel or accepted same-device layouts. The three rendering-record updates are supported by reproduced hashes and a controlled reversal of the earlier scheduler change.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100, Python 3.10, Torch 2.11 and CuTe DSL 4.7: 25 tests passed, 164 deselected. Covered BF16/FP16, one/two operands, HND/NHD/unified pools, int32/int64 slots, padded and out-of-range entries, and the updated mismatched-binding test. All live rows and untouched sentinels matched the bitwise reference. Nine additional real-tensor CPU/second-GPU cases reject before the compiled call, including pool_a. Four same-device one/two-operand preflight controls pass. In a safe negative control, the previous launcher reached an intercepted call for all nine invalid cases. No invalid-pointer kernel was launched. The two devices were SM100 and H100; this checks operand placement, not native execution on both devices. Both rendering tests passed under public DSL 4.8.0: all 13 sm_100a/sm_107a cubin hashes match. A private counterfactual reverting #1547's dense reader-credit alias and scheduler publisher predicate restores the three old dense hashes while preserving two THD controls. This attributes the record updates to that intentional body change; these are trace-compilation results, not native SM107 correctness tests. A bounded interleaved host-only comparison, with the compiled call intercepted, measured median preflight time of 14.18 us before and 15.47 us after, about 1.30 us added. No GPU or end-to-end performance claim. Reviewed all three changed files, existing served-route device checks and current-base interactions. Precheck found no candidates; the barrier ledger is empty because the kernel body is unchanged (checklist D10/D13/E01). Current-head Style and merge-metadata checks passed. Added the applicable area:global_attention label, preserving the existing FROST/bugfix/origin labels and Frontend 1.32.0 milestone.

Limitations: No native SM107 or full gated-block pipeline qualification. The numerical checks above cover the changed standalone launcher; the hash checks establish rendering identity only. CI is not yet evidence for this head. The smallest documented target covering the cache-write suite is python/*/cutedsl; its supported-DSL SM107 lane and older-DSL compatibility lanes will be tracked separately.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
